```{r}
# Read your data (replace with actual path or read.csv() if needed)
df <- read.csv("C:/Users/vreid/Downloads/for bootstrapping - Sequential (2).csv")
df <- as.data.frame(df)  

# Select columns relevant for draws
draw_cols <- c("X1st.Draw",    "X2nd.Draw"  ,  "X3rd.Draw"  ,  "X4th.Draw" ,  
  "X5th.Draw"  ,  "X6th.Draw"  ,  "X7th.Draw"  ,  "X8th.Draw"   , "X9th.Draw" ,   "X10th.Draw")

# Make long format
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("X"),  # Select all columns that start with "X"
               names_to = "Draw",
               values_to = "Lead") %>%
  mutate(Draw_Num = as.numeric(str_extract(Draw, "\\d+")))

# Determine time to event: first draw where Lead > 15
surv_data <- df_long %>%
  group_by(Address) %>%
  arrange(Draw_Num) %>%
  summarise(
    time = if(any(Lead > 10, na.rm = TRUE)) min(Draw_Num[Lead > 10], na.rm = TRUE) else max(Draw_Num, na.rm = TRUE),
    event = any(Lead > 10, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

depends on if next also more 10
```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

# Ensure column names are clean
names(df) <- make.names(names(df))

# Convert to long format
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("X"),  # Select all time-point draw columns
               names_to = "Draw",
               values_to = "Lead") %>%
  mutate(Draw_Num = as.numeric(str_extract(Draw, "\\d+"))) %>%
  arrange(Address, Draw_Num)  # Ensure ordering by address and draw number
df_long$Lead=as.numeric(df_long$Lead)
# Create a survival object
df_long <- df_long %>%
  mutate(Event = ifelse(Lead > 10, 1, 0))  # 1 if Lead > 15, else 0

# Fit the survival model
fit <- survfit(Surv(Draw_Num, Event) ~ 1, data = df_long)

# Plot
ggsurvplot(fit,
           conf.int = TRUE,
           title = "Time to Lead Level > 10 µg/L",
           xlab = "Draw Number",
           ylab = "Probability of Lead Level ≤ 10")

summary(fit)

# Calculate the mean survival time
mean_survival_time <- mean(fit$time)  # or fit$surv for the survival probabilities

# Print the mean survival time
print(mean_survival_time)


summary(fit)$table
```

after 10 always 1
```{r}
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

# Clean column names
names(df) <- make.names(names(df))

# Long format
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("X"),
               names_to = "Draw",
               values_to = "Lead") %>%
  mutate(Draw_Num = as.numeric(str_extract(Draw, "\\d+"))) %>%
  arrange(Address, Draw_Num)
df_long$Lead=as.numeric(df_long$Lead)
# Set Event to 1 at first Draw > 10, and stay 1 after
df_long <- df_long %>%
  group_by(Address) %>%
  mutate(First_Exceed_Draw = min(Draw_Num[Lead > 10], na.rm = TRUE),
         First_Exceed_Draw = ifelse(is.infinite(First_Exceed_Draw), NA, First_Exceed_Draw),  # Handle if never exceeded 10
         Event = ifelse(!is.na(First_Exceed_Draw) & Draw_Num >= First_Exceed_Draw, 1, 0)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Fit survival model
fit <- survfit(Surv(Draw_Num, Event) ~ 1, data = df_long)

# Plot survival curve
ggsurvplot(fit,
           conf.int = TRUE,
           title = "Time to Reaching Lead Level > 10ppb (and Beyond)",
           xlab = "Draw Number",
           ylab = "Probability of Not Yet 10ppb")

# Mean survival time (time to exceed 10)
mean_survival_time <- mean(fit$time)
print(mean_survival_time)
summary(fit)


summary(fit)$table


```

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

# Ensure column names are clean
names(df) <- make.names(names(df))

# Convert to long format
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("X"),  # Select all time-point draw columns
               names_to = "Draw",
               values_to = "Lead") %>%
  mutate(Draw_Num = as.numeric(str_extract(Draw, "\\d+"))) %>%
  arrange(Address, Draw_Num)
df_long$Lead=as.numeric(df_long$Lead)
# Create Event = 1 if this draw's Lead is the maximum for that Address
df_long <- df_long %>%
  group_by(Address, Date.Sampled) %>%
  mutate(
    P90_Lead = quantile(Lead, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE),
    Event = ifelse(Lead >= P90_Lead, 1, 0)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Fit the survival model
fit <- survfit(Surv(Draw_Num, Event) ~ 1, data = df_long)

# Plot the survival curve
ggsurvplot(fit,
           conf.int = TRUE,
           title = "Time to Max Lead Level per Address",
           xlab = "Draw Number",
           ylab = "Probability of Not Yet Reaching Max Lead Level")

# Summary
summary(fit)

# Calculate the mean survival time
mean_survival_time <- mean(fit$time)
print(mean_survival_time)

summary(fit)$table

```

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(survival)
library(survminer)

# Clean column names
names(df) <- make.names(names(df))

# Convert to long format
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("X"),
               names_to = "Draw",
               values_to = "Lead") %>%
  mutate(Draw_Num = as.numeric(str_extract(Draw, "\\d+"))) %>%
  arrange(Address, Draw_Num)
df_long$Lead=as.numeric(df_long$Lead)
# Identify first Draw_Num where max Lead is reached, and set Event = 1 at that point and after
df_long <- df_long %>%
  group_by(Address, Date.Sampled) %>%
  mutate(Max_Lead  = quantile(Lead, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE),
    Event = ifelse(Lead >= Max_Lead, 1, 0),
         Event = ifelse(Draw_Num >= Event, 1, 0)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Fit survival model
fit <- survfit(Surv(Draw_Num, Event) ~ 1, data = df_long)

# Plot survival curve
ggsurvplot(fit,
           conf.int = TRUE,
           title = "Time to Reaching Max Lead Level (and Beyond)",
           xlab = "Draw Number",
           ylab = "Probability of Not Yet Reaching Max Lead")

# Print mean survival time
mean_survival_time <- mean(fit$time)
print(mean_survival_time)
summary(fit)$table
```

```{r}
           conf.int = TRUE,
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# Reshape to long format
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("X"), names_to = "Draw", values_to = "Lead") %>%
  filter(str_detect(Draw, "Draw")) %>%  # Keep only draw columns
  mutate(Draw_Num = as.numeric(str_extract(Draw, "\\d+"))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Lead))

# Calculate average lead per draw
avg_lead_by_draw <- df_long %>%
  group_by(Draw_Num) %>%
  summarise(mean_lead = mean(Lead, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_lead = sd(Lead, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n(),
            se = sd_lead / sqrt(n))

# Plot
ggplot(avg_lead_by_draw, aes(x = Draw_Num, y = mean_lead)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_lead - se, ymax = mean_lead + se), width = 0.2, color = "gray40") +
  labs(title = "Average Lead Level Over Sequential Draws",
       x = "Draw Number",
       y = "Average Lead Level (µg/L)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Find the max value for each row across selected columns
df <- df %>%
  rowwise() %>%  # Process each row individually
  mutate(MaxValue = max(c_across(starts_with("X")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%  # Get max of selected columns (start with "X")
  ungroup()  # Remove rowwise grouping

# Check the result
head(df)
```

```{r}
# Create an empty vector to store the MaxSource column for each row
max_source <- vector("character", length = nrow(df))

# Iterate over each row to find the column with the MaxValue
for (i in 1:nrow(df)) {
  # Get the names of columns that start with "X"
  x_columns <- grep("^X", names(df), value = TRUE)
  
  # Get the row's values for columns starting with "X"
  row_values <- df[i, x_columns, drop = FALSE]
  
  # Find the column with the maximum value (that matches MaxValue)
  max_column <- which(row_values == df$MaxValue[i])
  
  # Store the column name corresponding to the max value
  if (length(max_column) > 0) {  # Ensure there is a match
    max_source[i] <- names(row_values)[max_column]
  } else {
    max_source[i] <- NA  # In case there's no match (this shouldn't happen)
  }
}

# Add the MaxSource column to the dataframe
df$MaxSource <- max_source

# Check the result
head(df)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

df <- df %>%
  select(-ends_with(".Minute"))  # This removes any columns ending with .Minute


# Step 1: Create MaxSource column (where max lead came from per address)
df <- df %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    MaxSource = if (all(is.na(as.numeric(c_across(starts_with("X")))))) {
      NA_character_
    } else {
      # Convert the values to numeric and find the max
      max_vals <- as.numeric(c_across(starts_with("X")))
      max_col <- which.max(max_vals)  # Index of the column with the highest value
      
      # Return the full column name (e.g., "X1", "X2", or "X3")
      names(.)[max_col]
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup()



# Step 2: Convert to long format
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("X"), 
               names_to = "Draw", 
               values_to = "Lead") %>%
  mutate(Draw_Num = as.numeric(str_extract(Draw, "\\d+")),
         Lead = as.numeric(Lead))

# Step 3: Join MaxSource to long data
df_long <- df_long %>%
  left_join(df %>% select(MaxSource), by = row_number())

# Step 4: Summarize lead levels by draw and MaxSource
avg_lead_by_draw <- df_long %>%
  group_by(MaxSource, Draw_Num) %>%
  summarise(mean_lead = mean(Lead, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_lead = sd(Lead, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n(),
            se = sd_lead / sqrt(n),
            .groups = "drop")

# Step 5: Plot grouped by MaxSource
ggplot(avg_lead_by_draw, aes(x = Draw_Num, y = mean_lead)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_lead - se, ymax = mean_lead + se), width = 0.2, color = "gray40") +
  facet_wrap(~ MaxSource) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Lead Level by Draw, Grouped by MaxSource",
    x = "Draw Number",
    y = "Average Lead Level (µg/L)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}

# Load required packages
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(forecast)

# Assuming df2 is already cleaned and you have a 'Max' variable



# Create a Date column for time series object (you can use Year and Month to construct it)
df2_monthly <- df_percentiles %>%
  mutate(Date = make_date(Year, Month, 1))
df2_monthly = drop_na(df2_monthly)

# Step 2: Create time series object
ts_data <- ts(df2_monthly$Percentile_90, start = c(min(df2_monthly$Year), min(df2_monthly$Month)), frequency = 12)

# Step 3: Check for stationarity (optional but recommended)
# Augmented Dickey-Fuller test (ADF) to check for stationarity
adf_test <- adf.test(ts_data)

# If p-value is high, the series is non-stationary and may require differencing
# For example, if stationarity is not found, apply differencing

# Step 4: Fit the SIRMA model (Seasonal ARIMA)
fit_sirma <- auto.arima(ts_data, seasonal = TRUE, stepwise = FALSE, approximation = FALSE)

# Step 5: Check the model summary
summary(fit_sirma)

# Step 6: Forecast the future
forecast_horizon <- 12  # Number of months to forecast (adjust as needed)
forecast_values <- forecast(fit_sirma, h = forecast_horizon)

# Plot the forecast
autoplot(forecast_values) + 
  ggtitle("SIRMA Model Forecast") + 
  xlab("Year") + ylab("Monthly Max Lead Level")

# Optionally, you can check the residuals of the model to ensure it fits well
checkresiduals(fit_sirma)

```

```{r}
# Load required packages
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(forecast)
library(ggplot2)

# Assuming df2 is already cleaned and you have a 'Max' variable



# Step 3: Check for stationarity (optional but recommended)
# Augmented Dickey-Fuller test (ADF) to check for stationarity
adf_test <- adf.test(ts_data)

# If p-value is high, the series is non-stationary and may require differencing
if (adf_test$p.value > 0.05) {
  ts_data_diff <- diff(ts_data)  # Apply differencing to make the series stationary
  # Now the series is stationary, check the ADF test again after differencing
  adf_test_diff <- adf.test(ts_data_diff)
  print(adf_test_diff)  # To check the ADF test after differencing
} else {
  ts_data_diff <- ts_data
}

# Step 4: Fit the SIRMA model (Seasonal ARIMA)
fit_sirma <- auto.arima(ts_data_diff, seasonal = TRUE, stepwise = FALSE, approximation = FALSE)

# Step 5: Check the model summary
summary(fit_sirma)

# Step 6: Forecast the future
forecast_horizon <- 12  # Number of months to forecast (adjust as needed)
forecast_values <- forecast(fit_sirma, h = forecast_horizon)

# Plot the forecast with points displayed
autoplot(forecast_values) + 
  geom_point(aes(x = time(ts_data), y = ts_data), color = "blue", size = 2) +  # Add points for actual data
  ggtitle("SIRMA Model Forecast") + 
  xlab("Year") + ylab("Monthly Max Lead Level")

# Optionally, you can check the residuals of the model to ensure it fits well
checkresiduals(fit_sirma)
```

```{r}
# Step 3: Check for stationarity (optional but recommended)
# Augmented Dickey-Fuller test (ADF) to check for stationarity
adf_test <- adf.test(ts_data)

# If p-value is high, the series is non-stationary and may require differencing
if (adf_test$p.value > 0.05) {
  ts_data_diff <- diff(ts_data)  # Apply differencing to make the series stationary
  # Now the series is stationary, check the ADF test again after differencing
  adf_test_diff <- adf.test(ts_data_diff)
  print(adf_test_diff)  # To check the ADF test after differencing
} else {
  ts_data_diff <- ts_data
}

# Step 4: Fit the SIRMA model (Seasonal ARIMA)
fit_sirma <- auto.arima(ts_data_diff, seasonal = TRUE, stepwise = FALSE, approximation = FALSE)

# Step 5: Check the model summary
summary(fit_sirma)

# Step 6: Forecast the future
```

```{r}
df_percentiles <- df2 %>%

# Load required packages
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(forecast)
library(ggplot2)

# Assuming df2 is already cleaned and you have a 'Max' variable
# Map seasons to months
df2_monthly <- df_percentiles %>%
  mutate(Month = case_when(
    season == "Fall" ~ 10,   # Fall corresponds to September
    season == "Winter" ~ 1,
    season == "Summer" ~ 7,
    season == "Spring"~ 4,# Winter corresponds to December
    TRUE ~ NA_real_         # Handle any missing or unexpected values
  )) %>%
  mutate(Date = make_date(Year, Month, 1)) %>%
  drop_na()

# Step 2: Create time series object
ts_data <- ts(df2_monthly$Percentile_90, start = c(min(df2_monthly$Year), min(df2_monthly$Month)), frequency = 4)




# Step 3: Check for stationarity (optional but recommended)
# Augmented Dickey-Fuller test (ADF) to check for stationarity
adf_test <- adf.test(ts_data)

# If p-value is high, the series is non-stationary and may require differencing
if (adf_test$p.value > 0.05) {
  ts_data_diff <- diff(ts_data)  # Apply differencing to make the series stationary
  # Now the series is stationary, check the ADF test again after differencing
  adf_test_diff <- adf.test(ts_data_diff)
  print(adf_test_diff)  # To check the ADF test after differencing
} else {
  ts_data_diff <- ts_data
}

# Step 4: Fit the SIRMA model (Seasonal ARIMA)
fit_sirma <- auto.arima(ts_data_diff, seasonal = TRUE, stepwise = FALSE, approximation = FALSE)

# Step 5: Check the model summary
summary(fit_sirma)

# Step 6: Forecast the future
forecast_horizon <- 4  # Number of months to forecast (adjust as needed)
forecast_values <- forecast(fit_sirma, h = forecast_horizon)


# Plot the forecast with points displayed
autoplot(forecast_values) + 
  geom_point(aes(x = time(ts_data), y = ts_data), color = "blue", size = 2) +  # Add points for actual data
  ggtitle("SIRMA Model Forecast") + 
  xlab("Year") + ylab("Monthly Max Lead Level")

# Optionally, you can check the residuals of the model to ensure it fits well
checkresiduals(fit_sirma)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(survival)
library(survminer)

# Clean column names
names(finalidk) <- make.names(names(finalidk))

# Convert to long format
df_long <- finalidk %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Draw1", "Draw2", "Draw3"),
               names_to = "Draw",
               values_to = "Lead") %>%
  mutate(Draw_Num = as.numeric(str_extract(Draw, "\\d+"))) %>%
  arrange(Address, Draw_Num)

# Identify first Draw_Num where max Lead is reached, and set Event = 1 at that point and after
df_long <- df_long %>%
  group_by(Address, Date) %>%
  mutate(Max_Lead = max(Lead, na.rm = TRUE),
         Max_Draw = min(Draw_Num[Lead == Max_Lead], na.rm = TRUE),
         Event = ifelse(Draw_Num >= Max_Draw, 1, 0)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Fit survival model
fit <- survfit(Surv(Draw_Num, Event) ~ 1, data = df_long)

# Plot survival curve
ggsurvplot(fit,
           conf.int = TRUE,
           title = "Time to Reaching Max Lead Level (and Beyond)",
           xlab = "Draw Number",
           ylab = "Probability of Not Yet Reaching Max Lead")

# Print mean survival time
mean_survival_time <- mean(fit$time)
print(mean_survival_time)
summary(fit)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(survival)
library(survminer)

# Clean column names
names(finalidk) <- make.names(names(finalidk))

# Convert to long format
df_long <- finalidk %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Draw1", "Draw2", "Draw3"),
               names_to = "Draw",
               values_to = "Lead") %>%
  mutate(Draw_Num = as.numeric(str_extract(Draw, "\\d+"))) %>%
  arrange(Address, Draw_Num)

# Identify first Draw_Num where max Lead is reached, and set Event = 1 at that point and after
# Set Event to 1 at first Draw > 10, and stay 1 after
df_long <- df_long %>%
  group_by(Address, Date) %>%
  mutate(First_Exceed_Draw = min(Draw_Num[Lead > 10], na.rm = TRUE),
         First_Exceed_Draw = ifelse(is.infinite(First_Exceed_Draw), NA, First_Exceed_Draw),  # Handle if never exceeded 10
         Event = ifelse(!is.na(First_Exceed_Draw) & Draw_Num >= First_Exceed_Draw, 1, 0)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Fit survival model
fit <- survfit(Surv(Draw_Num, Event) ~ 1, data = df_long)

# Plot survival curve
ggsurvplot(fit,
           conf.int = TRUE,
           title = "Time to Reaching Max Lead Level (and Beyond)",
           xlab = "Draw Number",
           ylab = "Probability of Not Yet Reaching Max Lead")

# Print mean survival time
mean_survival_time <- mean(fit$time)
print(mean_survival_time)

# Print the summary of the fit
summary(fit)

```
